q: Which famous queen of ancient Egypt was linked with Julius Caesar and Mark Antony?
fact: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

q: Which Tudor queen was known as 'the Virgin Queen'?
fact: Elizabeth I spoke several languages, including French, Italian, Latin and Greek.

q: Which explorer famously sailed across the Atlantic to the Americas in 1492?
fact: Columbus was born in Genoa, in what is now Italy, but his famous voyage was paid for by Spain.

q: Gladiators performed in arenas in which ancient civilisation?
fact: Some gladiators were so popular that fans scratched graffiti about them onto walls in Pompeii.

q: Which seafarers from Scandinavia sailed in longships?
fact: There's no evidence Vikings wore horned helmets; that idea became popular in the 1800s.

q: What was the main language of the ancient Romans?
fact: Homo sapiens, the scientific name for humans, is Latin for 'wise man'.

q: Which famous nurse was known as 'the Lady with the Lamp'?
fact: Florence Nightingale was also a gifted statistician who used diagrams to present her findings.

q: What were the kings of ancient Egypt called?
fact: The word 'pharaoh' comes from an Egyptian term meaning 'great house', first used for the royal palace.

q: Which famous prehistoric stone circle stands on Salisbury Plain?
fact: Stonehenge's smaller 'bluestones' were brought about 150 miles from the Preseli Hills in Wales.

q: Which scientist is said to have been inspired by a falling apple to think about gravity?
fact: Newton's famous apple tree still grows at Woolsthorpe Manor, his childhood home in Lincolnshire.

q: In medieval times, what was a large fortified home with a moat and drawbridge?
fact: Windsor Castle is said to be the oldest and largest occupied castle in the world.

q: Which Roman leader gave his name to the month of July?
fact: Before it was renamed, July was called Quintilis, meaning 'fifth month'.

q: What did the Romans build to carry fresh water into their towns?
fact: The Pont du Gard, a Roman aqueduct bridge in southern France, is nearly 50 metres tall.

q: According to legend, which king gathered his knights around a Round Table?
fact: In the legends, Arthur's court was at Camelot and his magical sword was called Excalibur.

q: In which forest is Robin Hood said to have lived?
fact: In the legends, Robin Hood's band of Merry Men included Little John and Friar Tuck.

q: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
fact: Richard Arkwright's Cromford Mill in Derbyshire, begun in 1771, was one of the first modern factories.

q: Ancient Egyptians wrote on a paper-like material made from which plant?
fact: Our word 'paper' comes from 'papyrus', a reed that grew along the River Nile.

q: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the USA as a gift?
fact: The Statue of Liberty was a shiny copper-brown colour at first and slowly turned green as it weathered.

q: The Penny Black was the world's first what?
fact: The Penny Black, issued in 1840, showed a side view of the young Queen Victoria.

q: Which ancient people built the Parthenon?
fact: The Parthenon's columns bulge very slightly in the middle so they look perfectly straight from afar.

q: What was the metal suit worn by medieval knights called?
fact: A full suit of plate armour usually weighed about 15 to 25 kg, spread across the whole body.

q: Which garment, a long draped piece of cloth, was worn by men in ancient Rome?
fact: Togas were usually made of wool and could be several metres long.

q: In Roman numerals, which number does X stand for?
fact: Roman numerals had no symbol for zero.

q: Which British monarch was the first to celebrate a Platinum Jubilee?
fact: A lemon Swiss roll and amaretti trifle won the Platinum Pudding competition for the 2022 Jubilee.

q: Which age came straight after the Stone Age?
fact: Bronze is made by mixing copper with a smaller amount of tin.

q: The Great Sphinx of Giza has the body of which animal?
fact: The Great Sphinx was carved out of a single mass of limestone bedrock.

q: The Model T was a famous early car made by which company?
fact: Henry Ford said customers could have a Model T in any colour 'so long as it is black'.

q: What is another name for the Middle Ages?
fact: 'Medieval' comes from the Latin 'medium aevum', meaning 'middle age'.

q: Which famous Paris landmark was built for the World's Fair of 1889?
fact: The Eiffel Tower was originally only meant to stand for 20 years.

q: Who was Queen Elizabeth II's husband?
fact: Elizabeth and Philip married at Westminster Abbey in 1947.

q: Which scientist came up with the theory of relativity?
fact: Einstein's most famous equation, E = mc², shows how energy and mass are linked.

q: Which country was once ruled by tsars?
fact: The word 'tsar' comes from 'Caesar', the title used by Roman emperors.

q: Samurai were the famous warriors of which country?
fact: Samurai often carried two swords: a long katana and a shorter one called a wakizashi.

q: Which Scottish scientist discovered penicillin?
fact: Fleming spotted penicillin in 1928 after mould grew on a dish he had left out in his lab.

q: Which famous playwright lived during the reign of Elizabeth I?
fact: Many of Shakespeare's plays were performed at the Globe, on the south bank of the Thames.
